platform.Platform: Initialize Limen before creating windows or graphics objects. Use GraphicsDriver.None for a platform-only app. Drive the event loop with pollEvent or processEvents, release application-owned resources, then call quit.
platform.Platform.init: Starts SDL and selects a graphics backend. Limen may select a different supported backend if the preferred one fails. Read graphicsDriver before creating a renderer.
platform.Platform.graphicsDriver: The backend Limen actually loaded. Use it to choose which renderer to initialize. GraphicsDriver.None also represents platform-only mode.
platform.Platform.videoBackend: The active SDL window-system backend. Check it before using backend-specific features such as Wayland or Win32 interop.
platform.Platform.isMobile: Whether Limen detected a mobile platform during initialization.
platform.Platform.setHint: Sets an SDL setting from SDLHint. Set hints that affect initialization before starting the subsystem they configure.
platform.Platform.addEventWatchListener: Adds a callback on the SDL event producer thread. Synchronize shared state and keep calling pollEvent to pump and drain the main queue.
platform.Platform.removeEventWatchListener: Unregisters a callback. Pass the same listener you registered.
platform.Platform.pollEvent: Copies the next queued event into target. Reuse one Event in your loop and read it only when the call returns true.
platform.Platform.processEvents: Drains queued events through onEvent. It returns false when the callback handles a Quit event by returning true.
platform.Platform.quit: Shuts down Limen and clears queued events. Release application-owned windows and graphics objects before calling it.
platform.Platform.getError: Returns current native error text. Read it immediately after a failing call to associate the message with that operation.

platform.window.Window: Owns a native SDL window. Use Window.create for named configuration. Attach a renderer if needed and destroy the window during shutdown. Use pixelWidth and pixelHeight to size GPU attachments.
platform.window.Window.create: Creates a window from named options after Platform.init. It is resizable by default. Add the backend's required flags before attaching a renderer.
platform.window.Window.new: Creates a window from positional arguments. Window.create lets you name options such as size, position, and flags.
platform.window.Window.id: The SDL window identifier. Compare it with Event.windowId to route events across multiple windows.
platform.window.Window.title: The caption shown by the window system. Assign a new value to update it.
platform.window.Window.width: The current width in window coordinates. Use pixelWidth for GPU attachments.
platform.window.Window.height: The current height in window coordinates. Use pixelHeight for GPU attachments.
platform.window.Window.pixelWidth: The drawable width in pixels. Read it after a resize to update the viewport or swapchain on high-density displays.
platform.window.Window.pixelHeight: The drawable height in pixels. Read it after a resize to update the viewport or swapchain on high-density displays.
platform.window.Window.windowToPixelRatio: The ratio of drawable pixels to window coordinates. Use it to convert window-space measurements for rendering.
platform.window.Window.minWidth: The minimum width constraint in window coordinates. Change it with setMinSize.
platform.window.Window.minHeight: The minimum height constraint in window coordinates. Change it with setMinSize.
platform.window.Window.maxWidth: The maximum width constraint in window coordinates. Change it with setMaxSize.
platform.window.Window.maxHeight: The maximum height constraint in window coordinates. Change it with setMaxSize.
platform.window.Window.x: The horizontal window position reported by SDL. Use setPosition to request a move.
platform.window.Window.y: The vertical window position reported by SDL. Use setPosition to request a move.
platform.window.Window.displayMode: The current WindowMode. Assign it to switch between windowed and fullscreen modes.
platform.window.Window.displaySetting: The display setting used when the window enters exclusive fullscreen mode.
platform.window.Window.currentMonitor: The display containing the window. Pass it to Display.modes or Display.currentMode.
platform.window.Window.visible: Controls whether the window is shown. Assign it directly or use show and hide.
platform.window.Window.opacity: Controls overall window transparency when the window system supports it.
platform.window.Window.grab: Controls input grab for this window. Release the grab when the interaction ends.
platform.window.Window.displayScale: The display scale reported for the window. Use it when adapting UI sizes to the active display.
platform.window.Window.resize: Requests a new size in window coordinates. Read the drawable size before resizing GPU resources.
platform.window.Window.setMinSize: Sets the minimum allowed width and height in window coordinates.
platform.window.Window.setMaxSize: Sets the maximum allowed width and height in window coordinates.
platform.window.Window.setIcon: Sets the window icon from a Limen Surface.
platform.window.Window.setIconICO: Decodes ICO bytes, applies the icon, and frees the temporary surface.
platform.window.Window.setIconFile: Reads an ICO file and applies it as the window icon.
platform.window.Window.getNativeWindowInfo: Reads backend-specific handles for native interop. Match the returned WindowNativeInfo variant before using its handles.
platform.window.Window.destroy: Releases the native window. Finish using its renderer and native handles before calling it.

platform.window.WindowOptions: Named configuration for Window.create. Provide title, width, and height for a basic window. Supply renderer flags when your backend requires them.
platform.window.WindowOptions.title: The initial caption shown by the window system.
platform.window.WindowOptions.width: The requested initial width in window coordinates.
platform.window.WindowOptions.height: The requested initial height in window coordinates.
platform.window.WindowOptions.x: The initial horizontal position. Omit it to request centering.
platform.window.WindowOptions.y: The initial vertical position. Omit it to request centering.
platform.window.WindowOptions.flags: Additional window flags. For OpenGL, include WindowFlags.SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL before creating the context.
platform.window.WindowOptions.resizable: Set to false to skip adding the resizable flag. Omit it to allow resizing by default.
platform.window.WindowOptions.visible: Set to false to create the window hidden, then show it when setup is complete.

platform.event.Event: Reusable payload filled by Platform.pollEvent. Switch on Event.type before reading the corresponding fields. Copy values you need to retain before polling again.
platform.event.Event.type: The event discriminator. Use switch to select the relevant payload fields.
platform.event.Event.new: Allocates an event object. Reuse it on each iteration of the event loop.
platform.event.Event.windowId: The SDL window identifier carried by window-specific events. Compare it with Window.id.
platform.event.Event.mouseX: The pointer's horizontal position in window coordinates for mouse events with a position.
platform.event.Event.mouseY: The pointer's vertical position in window coordinates for mouse events with a position.
platform.event.Event.mouseXRel: Horizontal movement since the previous mouse motion event.
platform.event.Event.mouseYRel: Vertical movement since the previous mouse motion event.
platform.event.Event.keyCode: The logical key for keyboard events. Use scanCode when physical position matters.
platform.event.Event.scanCode: The physical key position. Use keyCode for layout-dependent keys.
platform.event.Event.keyRepeat: Whether a key-down event was generated by holding a key. Check it for one-shot shortcuts.
platform.event.Event.state: The WindowStateChange carried by a WindowState event.
platform.event.Event.dropFile: The dropped file path carried by a file drop event.

platform.system.dialog.FileDialog: Shows native file and folder pickers. Handle selection, cancellation, and errors through FileDialogResult.
platform.system.dialog.FileDialog.openFile: Opens a picker for existing files. Inspect the callback result before using any paths.
platform.system.dialog.FileDialog.openFolder: Opens a folder picker. Use the path only when the callback reports a selection.
platform.system.dialog.FileDialog.saveFile: Prompts for a destination. Write the file yourself after the callback reports a selection.

platform.system.dialog.FileDialogResult.Selected: The user confirmed the dialog. Read the selected paths and optional filter index.
platform.system.dialog.FileDialogResult.Cancelled: The dialog closed without a selection.
platform.system.dialog.FileDialogResult.Failed: The native dialog could not complete. Use the message to report the failure.

graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL: Manages an OpenGL context for a Limen window. Make it current before issuing GL calls and present after drawing.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.create: Creates a context for a window opened with SDL_WINDOW_OPENGL. Pass ContextOptions to request a specific version, profile, or framebuffer configuration.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.makeCurrent: Binds this context for OpenGL calls on the current thread.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.present: Presents the rendered window buffer. Call it after issuing the frame's drawing commands.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.presentMode: The active presentation mode. It may be absent before a mode is established.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.requestedPresentMode: The requested presentation mode. Compare it with presentMode to see what took effect.
graphics.renderer.opengl.OpenGL.destroy: Releases the OpenGL context. Complete context-dependent cleanup before calling it.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan: Bootstraps Vulkan in Limen. Create a surface for the window, then create a context with your renderer's required capabilities.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.createSurface: Creates a Vulkan surface for the window. Request validation during setup when debugging Vulkan usage.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.createContext: Creates the Vulkan context for a surface. The queueFamily reference receives the selected queue family.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.getCapabilities: Reads the context's supported capabilities. Check these before enabling optional rendering features.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.loaderApiVersion: The API version reported by the Vulkan loader. Compare it with instanceApiVersion to see which version the instance uses.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.instanceApiVersion: The Vulkan API version selected for the instance.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.Vulkan.validationEnabled: Whether validation was enabled for the active Vulkan instance.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkComma: Records Vulkan commands for a queue. Begin recording, encode the work, end recording, then submit it with the required synchronization.

graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandL: Records GPU work for a D3D12 command queue. Close the list before submission and wait for the associated GPU work before reusing its allocator.

graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc: Describes the dimensions, format, layout, sampling, and usage of a resource. Fill this before creating a resource or querying its allocation size.

graphics.postprocess.dlss.DLSS: Provides NVIDIA Streamline hooks for DLSS and related features. Check feature support on the selected device before setting options or submitting work.
graphics.postprocess.dlss.DLSS.getNewFrameToken: Gets the Streamline token for a frame. Reuse it when submitting that frame's constants, resource tags, and evaluation.
graphics.postprocess.dlss.DLSS.setTagForFrame: Associates resources with their Streamline roles for a frame. Supply the matching frame token and resources expected by the feature.
graphics.postprocess.dlss.DLSS.evaluateFeature: Submits evaluation after supplying the feature's frame resources and constants.

graphics.postprocess.fsr.FSR: Provides AMD FidelityFX features such as upscaling and frame generation. Check effect availability, create the required context, and release it during shutdown.
graphics.postprocess.fsr.FSR.getRenderResolution: Computes render dimensions for a display size and quality mode. Read the output width and height references on success.
graphics.postprocess.fsr.FSR.createContext: Creates an upscaling context for maximum render and output dimensions. Inspect the result code before using the context.
graphics.postprocess.fsr.FSR.dispatch: Records FSR work on the supplied command list. Configure the input and output resources in FSRDispatchParams.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageC: Describes a Vulkan image. Choose its format, extent, mip levels, samples, tiling, and usage before creating it.

platform.input.Mouse: Use these helpers for mouse capture, relative mode, or state outside the event loop. Use Event for individual movement and button events.
platform.input.Mouse.setRelative: Toggles relative mouse mode. Use it for camera or pointer-lock style controls that consume movement deltas.
platform.input.Mouse.globalState: Reads desktop pointer coordinates into x and y and returns the button mask.
platform.input.Mouse.relativeState: Reads accumulated relative movement into x and y and returns the button mask.
platform.input.Mouse.warpGlobal: Requests a pointer move to desktop coordinates. Support depends on the window system.
platform.input.Mouse.capture: Requests mouse capture so drag gestures can keep receiving mouse events beyond the window.

platform.system.Clipboard: Use setText and getText for ordinary copy and paste. Use setData and getData when exchanging bytes under an explicit MIME type.
platform.system.Clipboard.getText: Reads clipboard text. Treat a null result as unavailable.
platform.system.Clipboard.getData: Reads bytes under a particular MIME type. Treat null as unavailable and decode the bytes according to their format.
platform.system.Clipboard.setData: Publishes bytes under the supplied MIME type. Inspect the result before assuming they were copied.
platform.system.Clipboard.mimeTypes: Lists the MIME types the clipboard currently advertises. Select a supported format before reading bytes.

platform.display.Display: Enumerates displays and their video modes. Use Window.currentMonitor to query the display containing an existing window.
platform.display.Display.all: Lists the displays reported by SDL.
platform.display.Display.modes: Lists the display modes available for the given display.
platform.display.Display.currentMode: Reads the current or desktop mode for the display, according to the desktop argument.

graphics.renderer.opengl.resource.Buffer: Creates and updates OpenGL buffer objects. Bind the buffer to the target expected by the operation, or use a named-buffer method where supported.
graphics.renderer.opengl.resource.Buffer.bufferDataSize: Allocates buffer storage without uploading an initial byte array. Bind the destination first.
graphics.renderer.opengl.resource.Buffer.bufferSubData: Updates a byte range of the currently bound buffer without reallocating it.
graphics.renderer.opengl.resource.Buffer.deleteBuffer: Deletes the OpenGL buffer object. Stop referencing it from future draw commands.

graphics.PresentMode: Selects how completed frames are presented. Use VSync to synchronize with the display. Query the actual mode if your application depends on a particular presentation policy.
graphics.PresentMode.Immediate: Requests presentation without waiting for a vertical blank. This can reduce wait time and may allow tearing.
graphics.PresentMode.VSync: Requests presentation synchronized to the display refresh.
graphics.PresentMode.Adaptive: Requests adaptive synchronization when the backend supports it.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi: Describes a queue submission. It pairs command buffers with semaphores that order their work with earlier and later submissions.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.waitSemaphoreCount: Number of semaphores the submission waits on. Match the entries in pWaitSemaphores and pWaitDstStageMask.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.pWaitSemaphores: Semaphores to wait on before the configured stages execute.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.pWaitDstStageMask: The pipeline stage mask for each wait semaphore. Keep the entries in the same order as pWaitSemaphores.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.commandBufferCount: Number of command buffers supplied in pCommandBuffers.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.pCommandBuffers: Recorded command buffers to submit. They must be valid for the queue used by the submission.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.signalSemaphoreCount: Number of semaphores supplied in pSignalSemaphores.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.command.VkSubmi.pSignalSemaphores: Semaphores signaled by the submission. Later work can wait on them.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkBuffer: Describes a buffer to create. Set its size and usage according to the operations that will access it.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkBuffer.usage: The permitted buffer uses, such as transfers, indexing, or shader access. Include each use that later commands require.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkBuffer.sharingMode: Controls how queue families access the buffer. Supply the family indices when using concurrent sharing.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkBuffer.queueFamilyIndexCount: Number of queue family indices in queueFamilyIndices when using concurrent sharing.

graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL: Specifies how a Vulkan image subresource is laid out for a particular use. Track its current layout and transition it before using it in a way that requires another layout.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.UNDEFINED: Use as the old layout when the previous contents may be discarded, such as the first transition of a newly created image.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.GENERAL: A general-purpose layout required by some usages, including typical storage-image access.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL: Layout for color attachment access during rendering.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL: Layout for depth and stencil attachment access.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL: Layout for shader reads, such as sampling a texture after an upload.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL: Layout for the source image in a transfer operation.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL: Layout for the destination image in a transfer operation.
graphics.renderer.vulkan.memory.VkImageL.PRESENT_SRC_KHR: Layout required for presenting a swapchain image. Transition the image before handing it back for presentation.

graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ: Submits recorded D3D12 command lists. Use fence values to track when queued GPU work has progressed far enough to reuse its resources.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ.executeCommandList: Submits a recorded command list for execution. Close the list before passing it to the queue.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ.executeCommandLists: Submits multiple recorded command lists. Close each list before submitting it.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ.signal: Schedules a fence update on the queue. Use the value to track completion of work submitted ahead of the signal.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ.wait: Makes the queue wait until a fence reaches the specified value. Use it to order work between queues.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.command.CommandQ.getTimestampFrequency: Reads the frequency of timestamps on this queue so GPU timestamp deltas can be converted to elapsed time.

graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc: Describes how a D3D12 resource or subresource can be accessed. Use a resource barrier when changing between states that require an explicit transition.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.RENDER_TARGET: Allows writing to a resource as a render target.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.UNORDERED_ACCESS: Allows unordered access through a UAV.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.DEPTH_WRITE: Allows writing to a depth-stencil attachment.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.COPY_DEST: Allows this resource to be written by a copy operation.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.COPY_SOURCE: Allows this resource to be read by a copy operation.
graphics.renderer.d3d12.resource.Resourc.PRESENT: Transition the back buffer to this state before presenting it.
